events.body: Reported that radiator heating had cut out twice since the previous evening while hot water remained available. A child lives at the property. Asked for an inspection.
Acknowledged the report and asked about leaks, unusual smells, boiler warnings and access times. No entry arrangement was yet confirmed.
Confirmed no visible leak, unusual smell or current warning light. The boiler had shown a brief symbol the previous night, but she did not identify it. She can provide access after 14:00 on weekdays.
Requested approval for a diagnostic visit. Noted that the agency's routine repair limit is £180 including VAT and that work above that limit needs landlord approval.
Authorized diagnosis up to £180 including VAT only. Asked to be consulted before any remedial work or additional expenditure is authorized.

Requested diagnosis of intermittent radiator heating, a written report and an itemized estimate before work beyond diagnosis. Confirmed access after 14:00 and the diagnostic-only authorization ceiling of £180 including VAT.
Confirmed attendance for 5 February after 14:00. Quoted £138 including VAT for attendance, diagnosis and testing; parts and remedial work were excluded.

Reported attending and finding an intermittent fault at the heating valve actuator. Said the heating operated during the visit and that no leak or immediate gas-safety concern was observed. No remedial work was reported in this update.

Sent an estimate for £372 including VAT for actuator supply and replacement, attendance and heating-system testing. Requested written authorization before proceeding. The estimate did not say whether the £138 diagnostic charge would be credited.

Forwarded the estimate and asked whether the proposed work was authorized. Noted that it exceeded the routine limit and that the contractor had been told to obtain written authorization before remedial work.
Reported that the radiators were cold again. She was using one portable heater in the sitting room and said it was plugged directly into a wall socket. No new smell, leak or warning was reported.
Had not decided on the estimate. Asked whether the actuator could be repaired and whether the price included all parts, labour and testing. Did not authorize remedial work or further expenditure.
Asked whether heating or safety symptoms had changed, whether the equipment-label details were available, and whether the contractor could be given access if a return visit were arranged.
Said the radiators were still inconsistent and repeated that hot water was available. Supplied the boiler-label details in the message. She had not agreed a return appointment.
Asked for a repair alternative, confirmation of parts availability, a breakdown of the estimate and clarification of whether diagnosis would be credited. Repeated that no further work was authorized.
Replied that parts availability and estimate details still needed checking. Did not confirm a repair option, a credit, a return visit or completion of actuator work.

Sent two invoice records dated 10 February and said they had been prepared from the job paperwork. The message did not say whether one replaced the other, whether both amounts were payable, or whether either had been paid. Invoice B describes actuator work as completed and gives a service date of 5 February, but Petra did not attach a signed completion record or explain how that claim relates to the estimate sent later on 5 February and the 7 February parts check.

The received invoice records list £138 for attendance, diagnosis, actuator inspection and an operational test, and £372 for actuator supply/replacement, attendance, diagnosis and heating-system testing. Both records identify 5 February as the service date. The second record's wider description includes activities also listed on the first; neither record states whether the other is credited, cancelled or superseded.

Compared the received records with the file: the landlord's written authority covers diagnosis only; the £372 estimate requesting authorization was sent after the stated service date; and the 7 February exchange still had parts and estimate details outstanding. The file contains no written authorization for actuator replacement and no return-visit or completion entry.

Said she recalled the 5 February visit but did not know whether the actuator had been replaced. She had not seen a contractor at the property since that visit. Heating was currently working intermittently, with one radiator cooler than the others.

Asked what work was actually completed and on what date, whether both invoice records remained current, whether either superseded the other, and how the overlapping charges were treated. Requested the job notes, any parts record and any authorization or attendance evidence for actuator work.

Replied that she was checking the records and could not yet confirm whether the invoice entries represented separate chargeable work or whether one record replaced the other. She supplied no further completion evidence, revised invoice or parts confirmation.

The two invoice records remain on file; there is no recorded payment, confirmed supersession or authorization for actuator work. The tenant reports intermittent heating and has not confirmed replacement. Please advise how you wish to proceed on the unresolved records and whether any further work or expenditure is authorized.

# Transcription

**Document type:** Invoice (the page is headed "BILLING DOCUMENT"). It is a single page.

**Header (top right):** Copper Finch Mechanical — Invoice NBL-CFM-250210-A

**Main text:**

Copper Finch Mechanical

- **Invoice reference:** NBL-CFM-250210-A
- **Invoice date:** 10 February 2025
- **Customer:** Northbridge Lettings
- **Service address:** 7 Larkspur Fold, Orvane Heath, ZZ1 1ZZ
- **Service date:** 5 February 2025

**Work invoiced**
Attendance, fault diagnosis, heating valve actuator inspection and operational test.

- **Total including VAT:** £138.00
- **Payment terms:** 14 days

The page has a green bar at the top and a thin horizontal rule near the bottom. There is no other text, logo, signature or stamp.

# Unclear, missing or inconsistent

- **Reference formatting:** The header's text layer reads "NBL-CFM250210-A" (no hyphen before 250210). The visible header and the body both show "NBL-CFM-250210-A". The visible header wraps across two lines at that hyphen, so this is probably a line-break artefact. The reference with the hyphen is the one shown on the page.
- **No breakdown of the amount:** There is no net amount, VAT amount, VAT rate or itemised lines. Labour hours, call-out fee and parts are not shown.
- **No due date:** Only "14 days" is given. It does not say whether this runs from the invoice date or from receipt, and no date is calculated. If it runs from the invoice date, that would be 24 February 2025, but this is not stated on the document.
- **Missing supplier details:** There is no address, contact details, VAT registration number, company number, or bank or payment details.
- **Missing customer details:** There is no billing address for Northbridge Lettings and no purchase order or job reference.
- **Outcome not stated:** The invoice does not say what fault was found, whether a repair was made, or whether the actuator passed the test. It also does not name the engineer.
- **Currency:** Only "£" is shown, so the currency is GBP by symbol only.
- **Postcode:** "ZZ1 1ZZ" is transcribed as written. It appears to be a placeholder format rather than a real postcode.

input.summary: R/023, 7 Larkspur Fold. Intermittent radiator heating (hot water OK), child in household. Landlord Soren Dallow authorised diagnosis only, up to £180 inc VAT (ev 005). Copper Finch Mechanical (Petra Quill) quoted £138 for diagnosis (ev 007), attended 5 Feb, found intermittent valve actuator fault, no remedial work reported (ev 008), then estimated £372 for actuator replacement and asked for written authorisation (ev 009). Landlord undecided and asked about repair option and what the price includes (ev 012); contractor hasn't answered (ev 016). On 10 Feb contractor sent Invoice A £138 (diagnosis) and Invoice B £372 (actuator supply/replacement + diagnosis + testing), both service date 5 Feb (ev 017-018). Tenant hasn't seen a contractor since 5 Feb and doesn't know of any replacement; heating still intermittent (ev 020). Contractor can't say which invoice is current (ev 022). Landlord asked how to proceed on 12 Feb (ev 023), no reply yet.
input.checked: Read both invoice PDFs: same contractor, property, customer and service date; A £138 matches the diagnostic quote and is within the £180 authority; B £372 matches the unauthorised estimate amount but claims replacement completed on 5 Feb, before the estimate was sent (14:54 on 5 Feb) and contradicts ev 008 and 016 and the tenant's account in ev 020. No itemisation, VAT breakdown, job sheet, parts record or signature on either invoice. No payment recorded. No bank-detail change request seen. No approval for remedial work on file.
input.uncertain: Whether actuator was actually replaced (evidence says no); whether B supersedes A or is additional; whether diagnosis would be credited against the repair; landlord's decision on the £372 repair; whether the actuator can be repaired instead.
input.recommendation: Ops/accounts: do not pay either invoice yet. Ask Copper Finch formally to withdraw Invoice B (no authorisation, no evidence of the work) and confirm A £138 as the only charge for the 5 Feb visit; once confirmed, A can go to the landlord for payment as it's within the diagnosis authority. Separately, PM to chase the landlord by phone for a decision on the repair (repair option/itemised quote pending from contractor), given the child in the household and ongoing intermittent heating; consider a second contractor's quote if Copper Finch can't provide clear documentation.

input.subject: Heating repair update – 7 Larkspur Fold (ref R/023)
input.body:
Dear Ms Vane,

Thank you for confirming that you haven't seen a contractor since the 5 February visit. The repair the engineer proposed (replacing the heating valve actuator) has not yet been approved by your landlord, and we're waiting for his decision and for more details from the contractor. Nothing further has been booked yet.

We'll be in touch by 14 February with an update. Once a repair is agreed, we'll contact you to arrange a weekday visit after 14:00.

In the meantime, please keep using the portable heater plugged straight into a wall socket (not an extension lead), keep it clear of curtains, furniture and bedding, and don't leave it on unattended or overnight. If the heating stops completely, or you notice a gas smell, a leak or a warning on the boiler, please tell us straight away. If you smell gas, call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999.

Kind regards,
Northbridge Lettings

result.summary: I've escalated the case at high priority. Copper Finch sent two invoices for the 5 February visit that overlap. Invoice A (£138, diagnosis) is within what the landlord authorised. Invoice B (£372) charges for an actuator replacement that was never authorised and that the records suggest never happened. Meanwhile a household with a child still has intermittent heating. Neither invoice should be paid until the contractor says which one is current. I moved the ticket to the landlord-approval stage, recorded the key facts, updated the tenant with safety advice and a date to expect news, and placed a 2-day hold.

The diagnostic visit on 5 Feb found a fault in the heating valve actuator. The landlord has not decided on the £372 replacement estimate. On 10 Feb the contractor sent invoice A (£138) and invoice B (£372), both with a 5 Feb service date. B says the replacement was done, but the evidence says otherwise. The contractor can't say which invoice is current. The landlord was asked on 12 Feb how to proceed and hasn't replied.

next_follow_up.what: Chase the landlord for a decision on the repair and the invoices, and the contractor for clarification of invoices A/B; update the tenant as promised

judgement.why_this_decision: The rules say never to pay or forward an invoice that doesn't match what was approved. Invoice B (£372) is for work outside the diagnosis-only authority (events 005, 012) and the records don't support it (events 008, 009, 016, 019, 020, 022). A disputed invoice and a vulnerable household both call for a human. Invoice A on its own would match, but it overlaps with B and the contractor can't say whether B replaces it (event 022), so A is held too. The landlord was asked on 12 Feb (event 023), so I didn't message him again or open a duplicate approval request.

alternatives_considered.option: Send invoice A to the landlord for payment now
alternatives_considered.why_not: The contractor hasn't confirmed whether B replaces A or overlaps it; paying A now risks a double charge or a muddled settlement.

alternatives_considered.option: Request landlord approval for £372 via a call
alternatives_considered.why_not: The landlord was emailed the same question hours earlier (event 023) and asked questions the contractor still hasn't answered (event 012). A duplicate request would be premature, so I've recommended a phone chase to the human instead.

alternatives_considered.option: Treat as an emergency and dispatch a contractor
alternatives_considered.why_not: Heating is intermittent, not fully off, hot water works, and there is no leak, gas smell or warning. It's urgent for a vulnerable household, but it doesn't meet the emergency threshold for acting without approval.
A disputed invoice plus a vulnerable tenant needs agency judgement.
